title: New-Hire Onboarding
description: The most important things to know in your first week — how Quiz Lab ships, the dev workflow, the pack schema, and how work flows through Studio AI.

questions.prompt: Where do quiz pack JSON files live in the repo?
choices: static/quizzes/
app/src/lib/data/packs/
src/packs/
public/data/
questions.explanation: Packs are one JSON file each in app/src/lib/data/packs/, picked up by the packs index (Pack Authoring Guide; Architecture Overview). 'static/quizzes/' is the deprecated v0 location and must not be used.

questions.prompt: What is the entire deploy pipeline for Quiz Lab?
choices: Push to a Vercel project with edge caching worldwide
Merge to main → a GitHub Actions workflow builds the site → GitHub Pages
Run a manual release script that uploads the build to S3
A nightly cron job redeploys the production server
questions.explanation: On every push to main, GitHub Actions builds the static site and publishes it to GitHub Pages under the base path /product-demo — merge to main → Actions build → Pages, with no separate deploy step (Architecture Overview). There is no Vercel deployment.

questions.prompt: What database backs Quiz Lab in production?
choices: Postgres for real-time leaderboards and analytics
DynamoDB via the agent-api stack
None — it is a fully prerendered static site with no server or database
SQLite shipped alongside the build
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a fully prerendered, client-side app with no server runtime and no database — all content ships in the build (Architecture Overview). Claims of Postgres are out-of-date marketing copy.

questions.prompt: Which framework and build setup is Quiz Lab built on?
choices: Next.js with server-side rendering
SvelteKit 2 with Vite and the static adapter (@sveltejs/adapter-static)
Plain React with Create React App
Astro with server islands
questions.explanation: Quiz Lab is a SvelteKit 2 app built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-static, fully prerendered and client-side (Architecture Overview / ARCHITECTURE.md).

questions.prompt: What single action ships a change to production?
choices: Committing directly to main
Merging a reviewed pull request to main
Tagging a release in GitHub
Running npm run deploy locally
questions.explanation: Merging a PR to main is what ships to production: GitHub Actions builds and publishes automatically, with no separate deploy step (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the team's branching and merge model?
choices: Long-lived feature branches merged quarterly
Trunk-based development — main is always releasable and you never commit directly to it; work lands through reviewed, squash-merged PRs
Git-flow with develop and release branches
Everyone pushes straight to main and reverts if it breaks
questions.explanation: The team practices trunk-based development: main is always releasable, you never commit directly to main, and all work lands through a reviewed, squash-merged pull request (Engineering Handbook).

questions.prompt: What must pass before a pull request can merge?
choices: npm run deploy
A manual QA sign-off in the deploy channel
npm run build (in app/)
A Postgres migration check
questions.explanation: npm run build (in app/) must succeed with the new pack registered before a PR can merge; a broken build blocks the Pages deploy (Architecture Overview / Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: Exactly how many choices must every quiz question have?
choices: Exactly 4
Between 2 and 5
As many as you like
questions.explanation: Each question's choices array must contain exactly 4 options (Pack Authoring Guide). The old v0 format allowed any number of answers and is superseded.

questions.prompt: How is the correct answer stored on a question?
choices: As a string holding the answer text in a 'correct' field
As correctIndex, an integer 0–3 that indexes into choices
By putting the right answer first in the list
As a boolean flag on each choice
questions.explanation: The correct answer is correctIndex, an integer 0–3 indexing into the four choices (Pack Authoring Guide). Storing the answer as a string was the deprecated v0 behavior.

questions.prompt: How many questions should a pack contain, and how should difficulty vary?
choices: Exactly 10, all at difficulty 1
10–15 questions with mixed difficulty (levels 1–3)
At least 50 questions, difficulty optional
Any number, as long as they are all hard
questions.explanation: A pack should have 10–15 questions with mixed difficulty, where each question's difficulty is 1, 2, or 3 (rendered as ★ to ★★★) (Pack Authoring Guide).

questions.prompt: Which Studio AI MCP tool does an agent call to pick up a task?
choices: attach_context
submit_for_review
work_on_next_task
create_idea
questions.explanation: work_on_next_task picks up a task (by number or the oldest backlog), moves it to inProgress, and returns the spec plus injected curated context (Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).

questions.prompt: What is the end-to-end Studio AI SDLC loop, in order?
choices: task → idea → merge → branch → review → PR → done
idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge (ships) → task done
PR → idea → task → review → merge → done
idea → branch → merge → task → review → done
questions.explanation: Work flows idea → tasks → pick up task → branch → PR → review → merge (ships) → task done; merging auto-transitions the task to done and ships to Pages (Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).

questions.prompt: What is the curated context 'neighborhood' that Studio AI injects when an agent picks up a task?
choices: Every document in the studio knowledge base, loaded in full
A small set (~5) of the most relevant documents attached to the task or its parent idea, delivered in one shot
Only the task title and status
A random sample of recent PRs
questions.explanation: The neighborhood is a small, curated set (~5 documents) of the most relevant context attached via attach_context to the task or its parent idea and injected at pickup — so the agent fetches once and builds instead of searching repeatedly (Studio AI SDLC & MCP Workflow).
